title: Tidyra — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Sorting Station. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sorting Station
options.lineage: municipal waste-sorting stations and civic recycling signage
options.thesis: Storage as a public sorting station: every byte already belongs to a labelled container, and nothing leaves the site without a signed slip. It refuses the category's gauge-and-rocket dashboard, and refuses its opposite — the grey screen with one blue accent and a donut.
options.viewport: Top app bar carries the device name and its free figure in tabular numerals. Below it the sorting station itself: six horizontal enamel containers — Apps, App data, Photos, Video, Audio, Everything else — each a full-width bar whose fill is drawn at the one shared scale used everywhere in the app, labelled in condensed signage caps with its exact size right-aligned. Findings stack beneath as collection slips, each with what it frees. A single extended FAB, SCAN, sits over the navigation bar.
options.signature: The container row: one bar per category, filled to its true share of the disk, with a hatched zone marking the part Tidyra proposes to remove. The same bar, same scale, reappears on the approval screen showing what the plan would actually take off the yard.
options.risk: Municipal colour coding slides into cartoon wheelie-bins the moment a container becomes an illustration. It has to stay signage: flat enamel plates, stencil type, no drawn bins anywhere.

raised.raise: One shared size scale across every screen. A megabyte is the same visual length on the container row, in a list row, and in the approval total — never re-normalised per screen to make a small finding look worth acting on.
One visible module. Containers, rows, slips and the FAB all snap to a single 8dp armature; nothing in the app sits off-grid.
Tabular lining numerals wherever a size appears, right-aligned and exact — 756 MB, never about 0.7 GB.
Interchange markers. Where a file belongs to two findings at once — a duplicate that also sits in WhatsApp media — it is drawn once with an explicit junction mark, never counted twice in two places.

options.label: The Appraisal Room
options.lineage: archival appraisal, accession numbers and retention schedules
options.thesis: The phone as a collection under appraisal. Every file carries provenance and a retention decision; the cleanup is a deaccession list you sign.
options.viewport: A ruled schedule: each row an accession line with class, date acquired, last consulted and extent in exact bytes; the retention decision sits in the right column as a stamped word — KEEP, REVIEW, DEACCESSION.
options.signature: The retention schedule: findings presented as an appraisal ledger where the user stamps each line, and the stamp block is the approval gate.
options.risk: This is also where most considered utility apps land — buff paper, oxblood accent and typewriter numerals is a well-worn 'thoughtful tool' look, and it topped my own ranking, which is exactly why the roll did not hand it to me.

options.label: One Item, One Screen
options.thesis: Triage as paging: each candidate for deletion owns the whole screen, actions stack on a right rail, the next one is one snap away.
options.viewport: One duplicate photo fills the frame; size, date and source anchored low-left; keep, delete, open and skip stacked down the right rail.
options.case: Holds audience identification outright — every phone owner already knows this surface, and reviewing 2,277 duplicates one at a time is genuinely what it is for. Loses product clarity: it cannot show what is taking space, only what is in front of you, so the scan, the app list and the organiser all need a second world.
options.risk: A cleanup app that feels like a feed invites mindless swiping over deliberate approval — the opposite of the product's first principle.

options.label: Dense Module Mosaic
options.lineage: Japanese high-density web, boxed modules and utility-red tabs
options.thesis: Everything on one screen: every category, count, size and state tiled as small ruled modules, so triage never costs a scroll.
options.viewport: A mosaic of ruled modules — storage, apps, duplicates, installers, empty folders, unused apps — each with a red header tab, a count, an exact size and its state, packed edge to edge at small type.
options.case: Holds product clarity: this is a triage product and density serves triage — 235 unused apps and 2,277 duplicates are a lot to show, and this world shows them without three scrolls. Loses audience identification: on a phone at arm's length the tiny type and packed rules read as a bank statement, and the app ships to people who already distrust cleaner apps.
options.risk: At phone scale this fights Android's 48dp touch target floor; modules dense enough to be the point are too small to tap.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: metropolitan rail map as enamel mural
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: phone owners do not identify with a route diagram of their own storage, and a network of lines answers 'how do I get there', not 'how big is it'.
options.kept: Its interchange discipline — every crossing drawn as one deliberate, labelled junction — became the assigned direction's rule against double-counting a file that belongs to two findings.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.lineage: gridded type specimen on a visible construction grid
options.case: Fuses poorly: monumental cell-built letterforms fight dense file lists, and a visible construction grid answers no question this user has.
options.kept: Its armature discipline — every element snapped to one visible module — became the assigned direction's single 8dp grid with nothing off it.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: botanical plates at one fixed scale
options.case: Fuses poorly: a seasonal life-cycle has no counterpart in storage, and the cream folio is the softest corner of a world this product has no claim on.
options.kept: Its fixed-scale discipline — every plate at the same exact scale and ground so comparison is honest — became the assigned direction's single size scale across the whole app, the rule that stops a cleaner inflating small findings.

options.label: Ikeda Datamatics
options.lineage: black and white data field, barcode columns and sine lattices
options.case: Fuses poorly: with no colour there is no category coding, and strobing inversion is hostile on a utility people open while annoyed. It also reads as the tool-monoculture answer — a data field for a data problem.
options.kept: Its numeric discipline — data set as exact tabular columns — became the assigned direction's tabular lining numerals and its refusal to round a size into vagueness.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a storage cleaner ships, executed impeccably: a donut of used space, coloured category legend, a list of cleanable items with checkboxes, and one big primary button.
canonCard.viewport: Donut with the used figure in the hole, legend beneath, cleanable categories as cards with checkboxes, 'Clean 4.2 GB' pinned to the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other cleaner in the store — including the ad-funded ones the audience already distrusts.
